query: Something for the Fair {Every Artifice student is expected to have something for the Artificers' Fair. Yours is a clockwork wren that sings a little flat.|Fair entries again. Your wren now sings on key, mostly, and has started to hop.|Your fair entry has a name, a shelf and a temperament. The class has opinions about it.} {Your neighbour's entry, a self-pouring teapot, is pouring onto the floor.|Someone's entry has escaped and is hiding under the bench.|{season == "spring": The fair is weeks away and nobody is ready.|The fire buckets have been moved closer to the benches, on the faculty's orders.}} Tinker with your own {You adjust the wren's voice-reed by a hair and it sings a whole scale. The workshop goes quiet to listen.|The wren hops, sings and flutters, and nothing catches fire. That's the bar, and you've cleared it.|You get the wren to sing something nobody built into it. You don't know how. You write it down very fast.} {The wren sings one perfect note and then smokes. Your fingers are singed from catching it.|You fix the flat note and break the hop. The wren lurches round the bench like a drunk sparrow. You burn a thumb on the spring.|The wren sings, beautifully, and then won't stop. You have to pull a gear with smoking pliers to get some peace, and burn yourself doing it.} Rescue the neighbour's entry {You stop the teapot pouring, rebind its spout-charm and dry the floor. Your own wren waits, unfinished, all hour. Your neighbour will owe you for life.|You coax the escaped entry out from under the bench and fix its leg. Your wren sulks on its shelf, untouched.|You spend the hour on someone else's machine again. Theirs works now. Yours sings flat.}
